Arhinful 18 November 2026 5:21pm Ranking Member on the Finance Committee of Parliament and a former Finance Minister, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has questioned the implementation of the government’s Big Push infrastructure programme, demanding an explanation for the progress of several projects despite significant budgetary allocations.
He said the programme’s performance record raised concerns about the government’s ability to translate its infrastructure spending commitments into completed projects.
Speaking during the parliamentary debate on the 2027 Budget, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee said the mid-year budget review showed that a significant number of Big Push projects had recorded little or no verifiable progress as of June 2026.
According to him, only 13 projects had reached at least 50 per cent completion, while 15 were between 25 and 50 per cent. He added that the status of 59 per cent of the projects had not been accounted for.
“Even with the Big Push that they have made so much noise about, when you look at the scorecard, it doesn’t tell a good story. As of June in the mid-year budget, this was the scorecard: only 13 projects of the Big Push had reached at least 50 per cent, and 15 were between 25 per cent and 50 per cent, and a whopping 59 per cent they could not even give account of their status,” he said.
Dr Amin Adam questioned how the government had utilised the funds allocated to the programme, asking: “So where has the money gone?”
He argued that the government needed to provide greater accountability for the resources committed to the infrastructure initiative.
